text:
aj: Thinking about our JS SDK publish strategy — we need to pick between shipping a single package with conditional exports vs two separate packages (esm and cjs). thoughts?

maria: single package + conditional exports feels cleaner for users but it's a pain to maintain build/test matrix. also typing entrypoints get weird.

sam: +1 on single package if we can automate checks. main concern is edge runtimes (Cloudflare/Vercel). they choke on CJS fields sometimes.

katie: For types: do we point "types" to dist/index.d.ts and add conditional exports for ./package.json#types? I've seen TS resolver use the "types" field even when exports hides entry. messy.

aj: Example idea: keep a single tarball but publish both dist/cjs and dist/esm and then use exports like: 
```json
"exports": {"import": "./dist/esm/index.js", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js"},
"types": "./dist/types/index.d.ts"
```
Would that work with bundlers and edge?

maria: That layout is pretty standard. pain points: node18 ESM interop, named exports, and Rollup/tree-shaking differences. Need a test matrix that runs on node, webpack, vite, and edge runtime.

sam: For edge: some runtimes only allow ESM. If package.json still has a "main" pointing to CJS, you can break deploys. But if exports covers it you're fine. Danger is older tooling that doesn't understand exports.

katie: Also think about typings: publishing a single index.d.ts root helps. Avoid conditional types entrypoints — TS doesn't support conditional exports for d.ts in all tsserver versions. I'd recommend a single unified types entry that re-exports specific signatures if needed.

aj: OK. What about CI/automation? We should gate publish on a smoke test that installs the tarball in a tiny app for: node cjs import, node esm import, vite (dev), and edge runtime (vercel dev).

maria: +1. Also add a types smoke: open a TS project that imports and checks types (tsc --noEmit). catches missing exports.

ci-bot: publish-preview job failed on the esm smoke test — bundler threw: "Unexpected token export" when importing package name in vite sandbox. (see logs: https://ci/reports/1123) :face_with_raised_eyebrow:

sam: probably our ESM build still has "type": "commonjs" somewhere or a stray CJS require. I'll grab the tarball and inspect.

katie: If we go single package, we should document migration steps for customers using require() in older Node. include runtime detection snippet and examples.

aj: Plan proposal: 1) single package with explicit exports import/require, 2) unified types entrypoint (dist/types/index.d.ts), 3) CI smoke suite (node/cjs, node/esm, vite, vercel dev, tsc), 4) a short migration doc. Anyone object?

maria: no objections. I'll draft the PR with the package.json changes + CI matrix. cc @katie for types re-export helper.

sam: I'll help debug the CI failing bundle. likely minor.

release-bot: FYI scheduled Canary publish for this branch at 2026-07-11T09:00:00Z (will run smoke tests).

katie: Sweet. I'll add a tiny TS repro to the repo so CI can tsc-check the tarball.

aj: thanks all. keeping this thread for the PR link and quick notes.
